author: tomas
text: stream_aborted = the chat socket closed while this socket's turn was in flight (reason connection_lost or closed, the latter when the app closed it e.g. leaving the chat). Error frames end the turn silently (no completed, no aborted). Turn state per ChatSocket so a StrictMode remount can't abort another socket's turn. Event attrs: model, ttft_ms / duration_ms / elapsed_ms, reason. No text, no ids.

author: tomas
text: D12 design: cross.yaml records the running api version from target_info (topk by latest timestamp, commit = first 7 chars of service_version), seat info from a pushed gauge build_commit_info{commit,seat,feature} (observability/build-runtime/commits.py reads board.jsonl, roster, usage.txt; pushes like teamstats), and p95 / error ratio / LLM cost per request overall and by commit. Delta = version mean over the range minus all-version mean over the same range. Build cost only from usage.txt (empty mid-sprint, never 0). Attribution: the seat of the latest handoff on the board key whose handoff or merge entry names that exact commit; else unattributed.

author: ansel
text: sqlcommenter: enable_commenter=True, commenter_options db_driver=False db_framework=False (comment = traceparent only, no version strings), asyncpg prepared-statement cache kept. Benchmark (specs/058-datastore-telemetry/bench_commenter.py, pg.py loopback, 3000 stmts each inside a span, 2 runs): off 485-490us median, spans 545-568us, commenter 1084-1087us (p95 1438-1503), commenter + cache off 1478-1482us. So +~0.53 ms per statement (unique text = one extra prepare); a chat turn's ~30 statements add ~16 ms against seconds of model time. Cache off is worse (every statement unnamed-prepared, no reuse at all), so it stays on. Off-path unchanged: instrument() only runs with telemetry on.

author: ansel
text: Found while benchmarking (pre-existing, 054): SQLAlchemyInstrumentor attaches TWO EngineTracers to every async engine (create_async_engine wrapper + the create_engine call inside it). Per statement one span is started and never ended (the second overwrites context._otel_span), and pool checkout/checkin events fire twice, so db_client_connections_usage (D6 pool panel) is likely double. With the commenter it also appends two traceparents; only the LAST one is the exported span, so 058's log parser takes the last. Not fixing in 058 (setup.py beyond my line is Nils's); repro: /tmp probe = instrument() then create_async_engine, print pg_stat_activity.query.

author: ansel
text: Docker access: no raw Docker socket in Alloy (it parses browser input via Faro). New always-on service docker-proxy (tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy:v0.4.1, socket :ro, GET only: CONTAINERS, INFO, VERSION, EVENTS; POST=0) on an internal network docker-api shared only with alloy and cadvisor; no host port. Note :ro on a socket restricts nothing by itself (the API still writes), the proxy's verb/path allowlist is the control. Residual: GET /containers/*/json shows other containers' env (DSNs) to Alloy.

author: ansel
text: cAdvisor: separate service cadvisor (ghcr.io/google/cadvisor:0.54.1, observability profile, no host port), not Alloy's built-in exporter. Probed on this host (Docker 29, containerd image store): cAdvisor needs the containerd socket to name containers (0.52 fails on layerdb, 0.54 without containerd.sock sees only the root cgroup). containerd.sock is root-equivalent, so it goes into a container that takes no untrusted input rather than into Alloy (Faro-facing; Alloy docs also ask for privileged). Mounts: /sys, /var/lib/docker, containerd.sock, all :ro; not privileged. Labels kept: compose project/service only; CPU+memory only (network needs host pid).

author: ansel
text: Exporter metrics travel prometheus.scrape -> prometheus.relabel -> prometheus.remote_write to Mimir /api/v1/push (WAL on alloy-data), not through the OTLP path: names stay the exporters' own (pg_*, redis_*, container_*), no job/instance->resource mapping. Every scrape keeps an allowlist of series names; job labels postgres, redis, cadvisor, alloy, loki, tempo, mimir; instance rewritten to a fixed name (never a DSN).

author: ansel
text: pg_stat_statements text stays out of metric labels (spec 9.3): stat_statements include_query=false, limit 100; track_utility=off (utility statements like ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD aren't normalized). D9's top-statements table is by queryid; log_line_prefix carries %Q so the slow-query log line in Loki (masked text) is found by the same query id.

author: ansel
text: Postgres log format: stderr with a parseable prefix '%m [%p] q=%Q %e ', not jsonlog (jsonlog needs logging_collector, which writes files in pgdata, not docker logs). log_parameter_max_length=0 (no bind values in duration lines; on-error already 0). Alloy: loki.source.docker (own compose project's db only) -> multiline join -> parse prefix -> otelcol.receiver.loki -> transform 'postgres' (resource service.name=postgres, last traceparent -> trace_id/span_id, then mask: all quoted strings, numeric literals in SQL, values after '=(' in details) -> memory_limiter (so stamp, redact, log_window, classify all apply).

author: ansel
text: Monitoring role: migration 0022 creates PG_MONITOR_USER (default wcl_monitor) LOGIN IN ROLE pg_monitor + CONNECT, only when PG_MONITOR_PASSWORD is set: no default password (unlike 0004's wcl_app). Unset = role skipped, exporter reports pg_up 0, app unaffected; README says how to add it later. Alloy gets the DSN from compose env (sys.env), shown as a secret in its UI.

author: ansel
text: Alerts: two Grafana-managed rules in provisioning/alerting/. (1) pipeline: send_failed + enqueue_failed + receiver refused for spans/logs (increase 2m) > 0; synthetic trigger = a log record Loki refuses for good (2 h behind its stream's newest -> 400). (2) build spend: estimated Claude Code USD over the last 24 h > threshold; the threshold is a constant recording rule alert:build_spend_usd_per_day:threshold in datastores.yaml (one place to edit, visible in Grafana; the test changes it in a MIMIR_RULES_DIR copy to go Firing -> Normal without restarts).

author: ansel
text: #76 root cause is NOT in the 058 scrape chain but in 055's otelcol.processor.transform "metric_labels" (config.alloy ~L180, outside my footprint). It deletes session.id/prompt.id/... from Claude Code datapoints; one Claude Code process exports a cumulative stream per session/prompt, so after the delete several datapoints in ONE OTLP request map to the same Mimir series with the same timestamp. Mimir keeps the first, counts the rest as sample_duplicate_timestamp, answers 200 and logs nothing (exactly #76). Reproduced on wcl-obs-ansel: one request with two claude_code.token.usage points differing only in session.id -> stored value 10 (first), cortex_discarded_samples_total{reason=sample_duplicate_timestamp} 1. Side effect: claude_code token/cost series keep ONE stream's value, so build spend (D-build, the spend alert) undercounts. My stack without Claude Code: 0 discards; raw cAdvisor output for every project on the host has no collision after the 058 relabel. Recommended fix (Maren's call, needs a grant): in metric_labels add a metric_statements block after the datapoint delete: aggregate_on_attributes("sum") where resource.attributes["service.name"] == "claude-code" (cumulative streams of one process sum to the process total at each export). Grant me metric_labels and I do it with a stack proof, or I ticket it. Meanwhile: datastores.sh asserts discards stay 0 for its run (no Claude Code there).

author: nils
text: #75 root cause found and reproduced (wcl-obs-nils, no app): it is NOT a second Resource in the backend (one Resource.create in setup.py, used by all three providers; ADK builds none). It is Alloy's spanmetrics connector: resource_metrics_key_attributes leaves service.version out, so each aggregate keeps the FIRST span's resource for as long as spans keep coming. The lead's backend first ran with WCL_GIT_SHA unset (compose default 'unknown'), then with fcef188: spanmetrics still exports target_info{service_version=unknown}, fresh. Repro: one span with version oldver, then 2 min of spans+metrics with newver -> two target_info series, oldver 12 s old. Same thing after every real redeploy (old SHA stays 'running'), so 'prefer != unknown' alone won't fix D12. Proposed fix (config.alloy, outside my footprint; Ansel holds it this round): a transform between otelcol.connector.spanmetrics and metric_labels, resource context: delete_key(attributes, "service.version") and delete_key(attributes, "vcs.ref.head.revision") (neither is a promoted label, so no spanmetrics series changes; only its stale target_info loses the version). And cross:running_version:info must read target_info{job="wcl-agent/api",service_version!=""} (Tomas). Maren: grant me that one transform in config.alloy (I prove it on my stack: after a version switch exactly one target_info with a version), or hand it to Ansel. I add the in-process test (every provider's resource carries the configured version) either way.

text: LIVE RE-CHECK 059-fix (WCL_PROFILES=1 via shell, WCL_GIT_SHA switched 70ba94d -> 9a4d860): PASS (1) Pyroscope span_name values = route templates + 'chat turn' only, no trace_id label; (2) after the switch target_info{job=wcl-agent/api} has exactly one series, 9a4d860; (5) PYROSCOPE_SERVER_ADDRESS set only with WCL_PROFILES. FAIL (3) D8 still has no failed-request series: 4 query embeddings failed ('query embedding failed, keyword search only: TimeoutError') and app_embedding_duration only has task=document. Cause: kb/search.py _embed wraps embedder.embed in asyncio.timeout(EMBED_TIMEOUT_S=3.0); the timeout CANCELS the provider call, so embedder.py sees CancelledError (BaseException) and its 'except Exception' never records; the TimeoutError is raised outside, in search.py. Fix: record in a 'finally'/'except BaseException' in embedder (error.type from the cancel -> 'TimeoutError' or 'cancelled'), or record in search._embed on the timeout. Also strong lead for sc-428 (semantic search always down): every search_knowledge took ~3.03-3.11 s = the 3 s query-embedding budget; Vertex gemini-embedding-001 query latency on this host is above 3 s, so the root cause is likely just EMBED_TIMEOUT_S too short (or a cold client per call). UNCLEAR (4) D6 node graph: only the wcl node shows avg response time, as '0.00 ms/r'; api/redis show none. Could be low traffic right after the Alloy restart or a seconds-vs-ms unit; Nils to judge from the panel query.
